original_card.question: Can one precisely specified helper-mixing word satisfy a replacement for the inherited H2/K interface?
methods: Derive a replacement interface lemma and price its implementation.
Seek an exact dirty-input or chronological-cut counterexample to the proposed replacement.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A full boundary contract and paid profile; unchanged scalar counts alone are insufficient.

first_step.inspect: Compare the two false H2/K flags with the unchanged paid profile in its README.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write one replacement H2/K implication for a single helper-star operation, then try to falsify it on dirty inputs.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A legitimate replacement could admit a cheaper bit circuit; scalar savings alone do not alter the selected moment.
allowed_variations: Choose one helper-star or quartet instance; narrow to one boundary implication.
scope_change_triggers: Changing only source count or scalar addition count without an interface argument.

actual_scope: One replacement H2/K implication (PR1194's H2-sem) audited on the PR848 copy-path helper-temp sharing wrap of the selected R439 word: the single pair 277->434 first, then the seed-42 greedy 205-pair matching, with dirty-input and chronological-cut falsification controls.
scope_change_reason: The card's first experiment is kept exactly (one replacement H2/K implication, falsified on dirty inputs); the instance is narrowed from a generic helper-star to the helper-mixing word the inherited H2 provably rejects (PR848 control C1), so the replacement is tested where the old interface fails. The allowed variation 'narrow to one boundary implication' applies; no source count or scalar-count-only change is made.
bottleneck_link: A legitimate replacement could admit a cheaper bit circuit: PR848 priced 6,231 D source reads of helper-sharing savings that gate-local H2 rejects; this audit decides only the interface admission, so scalar savings alone still do not alter the selected moment.
stop_rule: One implication, one matched family (single pair and the fixed seed-42 matching), controls complete; no envelope/pricing work after the interface question is decided.
evidence: CERTIFICATE.json and verify.py (7 controls); written implication statement and falsification table in README.md
author: Aaron Wang
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance from opencode; no independent human review.

open_questions.question: Do the admitted 205-pair and single-pair wraps satisfy the F/B positive envelopes, the exact local 104-bit and nine-stage 192-bit expressions and the paid-profile accounting?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The 6,231 source-read reduction becomes a real bit-circuit saving only if every billed guard still holds; identical binary endpoints do not bound intermediate integer envelopes.
open_questions.first_step: Rerun the bound machinery of research/r439-bsection-stars-seed01/verify.py on the wrapped D and compare F/B and both bit expressions.
open_questions.blocked_by: The envelope code is pinned in predecessor packages and must be reused unchanged; the helper-star word already sat at 99.996% of the nine-stage cap.

open_questions.question: Is H2-sem condition 2 (no target feeds a source or helper) necessary at the framed level, or does some weaker replacement admit the F4-shaped target-feeding wrap?
open_questions.why_it_matters: F4 preserves the full scalar operator and endpoint yet is excluded by the retained clause; a justified weakening enlarges the admissible wrap class.
open_questions.first_step: Extract the exact use of H1 in the interleaved lemma's block-triangular step and test the F4 word against that conclusion alone.
open_questions.blocked_by: The lemma's proof invokes H1 directly; an operator-level check cannot replace it without a new chronological argument.
